items.text: "Air Farce"
Charles River Bank, 1908
It's a beautiful day, and many people have gathered along the river to enjoy it. The spirit of this moment in time feels intensely hopeful.

Humans have conquered darkness with electric light and distance with the chug of locomotives. What will come next? Will they conquer the sky and beyond? If nothing else, they feel assured the future is bright.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Ladies and gentlemen, make way please!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Are the spotlights ready? I'll pay, Sam! Trust me, for once!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Thank you, sir. This won't take long, I promise. 30 minutes tops, and I'll be out of your way!
Victor has become one-part engineer and two-parts showman, frantically lining up equipment and impatient reporters at the same time.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: I promise you, gentlemen, soon you will possess the most memorable and valuable photos of the century. Forget the headlines of The Sun, this is history—

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Ah, pardon me. I need a moment to talk with my lovely assistant.
The engineer wipes off his fake smile as quickly as he turns, running over to help Lucy unload the metal frame.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The assembly time should be approximately five minutes.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Yeah, yeah, great—I just got a brilliant idea, Luce.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I am listening.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: We both know we can't afford another failure.
The engineer glances around and hushes his voice.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Our current model still has some problems to be solved, so why don't you just use that arcane skill of yours to "spruce her up," you know?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You mean you want me to change its mechanical structure to make the experiment work?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Yes, yes! E-exactly what I mean!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: No. I refuse.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: What? Why? What's ...

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: First, you must remember there are limits to my arcane skill. I may run out of time, and it is possible it will not work.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: The odds are already stacked against us in the first place! What could it hurt, even if it fails?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It would be impossible for me to enchant every suit once our model is put into mass production.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Without even mentioning that it would be impossible to enchant them each time they were needed.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Arcane skills simply do not work that way.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Our goal is a stable, reliable, and practical model. Who would buy anything less?
She focuses on the future, not the present, hoping to appeal to the engineer's true desire.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Now, you have my reasons. Please assist me with the wings.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Do you have that head of yours screwed on wrong? Or do you really not get that our project is done if we fail again?!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Luce, it's real simple: enchant the engine, go up and have a little fun in the sky, then come back down to greet the reporters when they come to take photos of you!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Our investors will change their minds. Hell, they'll beg us to continue. Then we'll have all the money we could ever want to make this hunk of bolts really work!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: And once we actually finish it, Luce, buddy, we'll have stacks as high as Rockefeller.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: OK. But why would we want a pile of paper?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: That's all I've ever wanted! Ever since I found these old drafts while cleaning up my old nan's house.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Your motivations notwithstanding.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: This project has a promising future. That is all I know.
Victor throws the drafts to the ground in a huff. Lucy picks them up and returns them to the car.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We still need these.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Like hell we do!
The engineer storms away, but as he enters sight of the crowd, he puts on his fake smile as cool as he can be.
It's smaller than he'd hoped.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Victor, please ask the crowd to disperse.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: There may be unexpected dangers. I do not want anyone to be hurt.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: You heard the lady, folks. My assistant is meticulously careful and considerate. Even though our invention is completely safe.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Still, as a practical humanist and a thorough scientist, she's always taking even the rarest and most extreme worst-case scenarios into consideration. But I do really have to emphasize "rarest."

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Now, ladies and gentlemen, let's witness the latest creation of Victor's Workshop: the fantastic wingsuit! Press one button and control the wings with a simple lever. That's all it takes to fly right up into the sky!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hold on, Victor. We are not quite ready.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: There is some turbulence in the air. We should delay for a short while until it passes.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Excuse us, friends. I'm afraid we need to adjust our equipment just one last time to make sure it all runs smoothly. Please, give us just two more minutes!

items.speaker: The Crowd
items.text: Hey, what circus are you from, pal?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Victor's Workshop of Boston, sir. We're not a circus or some arcane swindlers.

items.speaker: The Crowd
items.text: A pair of iron wings? Installed on a robot's back? Sure sounds like a clown act to me! Haha!

items.speaker: The Crowd
items.text: Go on, let's see it then! What can she do?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: We can't keep waiting, Luce. The crowd's turning on us.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I am on standby until the right wind arrives.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You appear anxious. Why is that?
A ship floats past them on the river, its passengers gawking at the scene.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Because, we need to take off now. Or all those very nice folk out there are going to leave, and our last chance for fame and fortune goes with them.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Is that so? What does that mean for the project?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: What good does that spotlight do for our experiment?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Will the people gathering by the river help us optimize our wingspan, our power source?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: You're being difficult. What's the point of this experiment if no one is here to see it?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The point? The point is that we put our work into perfecting this machine. Is that not point enough?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Even if something does go wrong, it will give us a chance to analyze and fix it. That is the point.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Humans have dreamed of flying in the wind since before even the first kite flew into the air.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: And now, our achievements in materials science and the development of the internal combustion engine have laid the foundation for us to make this dream a reality.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: What do we lose even if we fail again, Victor? We have failed a hundred times. What is so terrible about one more?
The engineer has no answer for her. The moment turns as a swift westerly wind blows across the river bank.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: That's your wind, Luce! Go on!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Move! Move! Good luck!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It is in the hands of fate now.
The mechanical woman pulls the device over her silvery arms.
Now a bird with iron wings, she walks to the edge of the river bank and presses a button as a jet of air erupts beneath her.
No signs of arcanum, only the mechanical rumble of human technology.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We have done all we can. I have a feeling that this time we will succeed.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: You ready?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Ladies and gentlemen, please direct your eyes—

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: For you are about to bear witness to the greatest invention in human history!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Where Icarus failed, we succeed. Now, mankind will take to the skies just as easily as the birds.
Like her friend ran toward the sea those many years ago, Lucy spreads her wings and leaps from the river bank.

items.speaker: The Crowd
items.text: Hey! That was a jump! She jumped!

items.speaker: The Crowd
items.text: Come on, do any of you think that stupid contraption is going to fly?
Where many expected a splash, they hear instead a roar, as the engine pulls her up and over the surface of the water.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: There appears to be some unexpected instability.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Look, look! She's rising, folks! That's no mere glide! But 100% genuine powered flight!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Up, and onwards!
The engineer stares out at the silvery bird as it holds just above the river's surface.
Sweat drips off his forehead, and the yellow draft paper in his hand is now a crumpled ball. But he turns back to the crowd.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Victor—

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Let me tell you folks. This thing is safe, stable, and reliable. Why even a child may pilot it after a few short lessons!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Imagine it, faster than an airship, more convenient than a locomotive, and cheaper than an automobile!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Victor!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Gentlemen, I ask you now for just a small investment. One small payment, to put yourself in front of the most important invention of our time!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: This is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to own a piece of the future! Seize it now! Fame and fortune await!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Victor! Something is wrong!
The engine begins to sputter and cough, no longer moving forward. The buffeting wind pulls her into a tumble.

items.speaker: The Crowd
items.text: Your future just took a nose dive, pal.

items.speaker: The Crowd
items.text: Oof, look how she hit the water! That could've killed somebody!
The engineer turns white, slowly wrenching his head toward the splash.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: No!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: No ...
The iron bird pulls herself up to the river bank and drops her wings.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I believe that I have found our problem.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Our engine is not providing sufficient downward thrust to keep us in the air, even with the aid of wind.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: There are also many extraneous parts. We could significantly streamline the design to improve our fuel efficiency.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: If we can improve the overall power output—

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Yeah, well, good luck with that, Luce. I'm out.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: No one is going to invest after today—Not a penny.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: It's a money pit, and I'm tired of digging it. No chance I'm going to see a profit, not in ten years, not in a hundred!
The mechanical woman dries herself and walks to the engineer as he mopes on the ground.
They deserve a better ending.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: So, you give up? We got this close, and you just want to walk away?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Seems like it, don't it?
Victor ends his last attempt with a heaving sigh. Pulling his hat down over his face, he walks out into the crowd and doesn't return.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: This is only another failed result.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We have found another avenue for improvement.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: This is nothing more than a minor setback. An unsuccessful experiment is not a critical failure.
The crowd is dispersing now, and Victor has disappeared with them. Flying is a beautiful dream, but dreams do nothing for a man with an empty wallet and a growling stomach.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You only ever saw what you could reach in one grasp, Victor.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But it takes more patience than that if you really want to touch the sky.
But he is gone; the random movement of fate has left her alone once more.
But that will not stop her.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Like many before him, he was terrified by the difficulties ahead and changed his course, like those mountaineers who turned from the Matterhorn long before they reached its peak.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But I know there will be others—those behind him—that will climb higher than he had ever imagined.
